title: Adaptive SDK compatibility playbook for pagination, retries, and streaming fallbacks
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Establish a language-agnostic playbook and concrete requirements for the Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs that defines pagination token semantics, retry idempotency, streaming chunk framing and fallbacks, and explicit back-compat rules. This PRD clarifies scope, enumerates trade-offs, and specifies acceptance criteria and testing obligations for engineering and SDK maintainers.

Scope (in): pagination cursor format and evolution policy; client-side retry semantics (idempotent vs non-idempotent actions); streaming API wire/frame semantics and 'graceful fallthrough' to polled/short-poll patterns when streaming is unavailable; per-language ergonomic surfaces and canonical error mapping.

Scope (out): language-specific idiomatic wrappers beyond the minimal ergonomic surface (e.g., fully reactive RxJS wrapper, coroutine abstraction libraries) unless flagged in follow-ups; server-side model contract changes (covered by separate runtime migration projects).

Goals:
- Provide a single source of truth for SDK teams and integrators about how clients should behave when encountering partial failures, model variants, or capacity fallbacks.
- Reduce customer-facing regressions caused by subtle token/cursor changes or streaming discontinuities.
- Ensure automated acceptance tests and SDK conformance checks validate compatibility across minor and patch releases.

Non-goals: force a single SDK implementation; mandate packaging/exports beyond public surface; lock server teams into a single token encoding format (we require a stable spec, not a single codec).

High-level decisions and rationale:
- Pagination tokens: tokens are opaque strings for clients, but the server must document a stable encoding version prefix (e.g., v1:, v2:) so SDKs can route to a migration path. SDKs must treat tokens as opaque and only carry/forward them; optional helpers to parse tokens are allowed behind feature flags. Rationale: minimizes client breakage while enabling server-side evolution.
- Retry semantics: SDKs provide three modes: safe-default (automatic retries for idempotent GET-like calls), conservative (no auto-retry except for explicit idempotent operations), and aggressive (best-effort retries including exponential backoff with jitter). The default shipping mode is safe-default. SDKs must expose an escape hatch for integrators to supply custom retry polices.
- Streaming: define a canonical streaming envelope and framing that supports incremental JSON objects and terminal metadata. SDKs must expose a streaming iterator/async generator and a fallback path that converts a terminated stream into a paginated poller when network conditions or gateways block SSE/HTTP/2 streaming.
- Backwards compatibility window: minor SDK releases must maintain behavioral compatibility for 90 days after release with escape hatches for customers to lock to older behavior. Breaking changes must be feature-gated and announced with a deprecation timeline.

Deliverables:
- This playbook (this ticket) and an associated conformance checklist.
- Language-specific implementation guidelines for Python/TS/Go written as short READMEs.
- Acceptance test suite (automated) covering token propagation, simulated partial streaming failures, and retry behavior under injected transient errors.

Open questions:
1) Should pagination cursors include region/cluster hints to enable smart routing? Trade-off: exposes server topology vs better client steering. Proposal: opt-in metadata prefix only when necessary.
2) Streaming backpressure semantics across languages (buffering vs drop): recommend unbounded user-facing buffers with configurable max queue size in language SDKs.
3) How to encode long-lived cursor version negotiation? Use a short version prefix in the token.

Reference artifacts:
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.company.internal/sdk-compat-playbook (working draft)
- Example GH PR (design discussion): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/642
- Runtime fallbacks design doc: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1abcDEF_example
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Python/TS/Go) treat pagination tokens as opaque strings; unit tests verify tokens are forwarded unchanged across pagination calls.
Server-provided token versions are detectable by SDKs via a vX: prefix; SDKs log a one-time notice when encountering an unknown token version and surface a clear error if migration is required.
Default retry policy (safe-default) retries only idempotent endpoints with exponential backoff and capped at 3 attempts; behavior is covered by integration tests that inject transient 5xx errors.
SDKs expose a configurable retry handler allowing users to opt into conservative or aggressive modes and to provide custom idempotency keys for non-idempotent actions.

Streaming API surfaces: SDK exposes an async iterator/Observable/chan that yields incremental JSON events; a standardized terminal object is delivered on stream completion with 'status' and 'final_token' keys.

When streaming is unavailable (network/proxy/gateway), SDKs automatically fall back to a paginated poller within 1s and maintain event ordering semantics; an integration test simulates blocked streaming and validates the fallback path.
Compatibility tests: a conformance suite validates minor SDK releases against a golden runtime behavior for 90 days; failing tests must be triaged within 5 business days.
Docs: language-specific READMEs with sample code for pagination, idempotency, streaming fallback, and a migration checklist are published under the SDK repo 'docs/compat-playbook'.
